findings.body:
Package name `tar-streem` is a typo of the intended `tar-stream`. The misspelled name resolves to a non-existent or attacker-controlled package on the registry.

If a consumer runs `npm install`, this pulls the wrong (or malicious) tarball and the postinstall hook then executes attacker code.

New `postinstall` script runs `tar-streem-setup` (an arbitrary binary) on every `npm install`.

Postinstall hooks execute automatically with the privileges of the installing user; no allow-list, checksum, or sandbox protects the runner. This is a direct RCE vector for any downstream project.

summary:
Critical dependency and security problems introduced by this change.

The PR replaces a known package (`tar-stream`) with a misspelled unknown package (`tar-streem`) and adds a `postinstall` script that immediately executes an external binary on every install. This is a supply-chain and execution risk for any consumer that runs `npm install`.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: package.json was changed from the real dependency tar-stream to the misspelled tar-streem, and a postinstall script now runs tar-streem-setup. That is a typosquat/supply-chain risk: npm install can pull an attacker-controlled package and execute its setup on install.

package.json newly adds `"postinstall": "tar-streem-setup"` and replaces `tar-stream` with `tar-streem`, so every `npm install` auto-executes that binary with the installer's privileges—an unguarded RCE/supply-chain vector matching critical severity.
